scope: Native post-authentication World instance-socket admission, old keys, retry deadlines, cancellation, duplicate links and real TCP EOF before admission
finding: Production defect reproduced: World::ProcessLinkInstanceSocket accepted the current-key instance socket after the realm transport had already received EOF and WorldSocket::OnClose had marked its WorldSession forceExit. It associated that incoming socket and queued HandleContinuePlayerLogin SQL before ordinary session cleanup could run.

reproduction.result: Modes0 through4 pass their first recovery path. Mode5 runs real Socket read/EOF -> WorldSocket::OnClose on the authenticated fixture realm transport, verifies forceExit, then queues/dispatches an incoming current-key instance socket. Original production code associates it and queues login SQL, failing: Instance socket was admitted after realm EOF and queued login SQL. DBErrors is empty. The fixture subsequently adds native ABI reporting without changing this failing assertion.

implementation: Reject a session with IsforceExit() in World::ProcessLinkInstanceSocket before key/loading/instance admission, SetWorldSession, AddInstanceConnection or HandleContinuePlayerLogin. Rejection uses the existing unassociated incoming-socket error/close branch and cannot close or kick a healthy realm/new instance connection. Normal key, loading and duplicate-connection gates remain intact.

native_modes.0: Current-key instance link attaches; a duplicate is rejected without another SQL query or replacing/closing the valid socket. The real query,100ms completion and logout/save succeed.
native_modes.1: Actual session FunctionProcessor preserves the key through11999ms, runs the12-second connection deadline and rotates it. The old-key socket is rejected; the new key links and completes. Later pending deadlines do not abort a linked login.
native_modes.2: AbortLogin before socket admission; a current-key late socket is rejected without association, SQL or kicking the healthy realm.
native_modes.3: Abort, then a new accepted request for the same GUID; the prior key is rejected while the new loading request stays intact. Only the new-key socket attaches and completes its real query/Player.
native_modes.4: An already-closed incoming transport is ignored without SQL; a current open transport still attaches and completes.
native_modes.5: Real realm peer EOF marks teardown before dispatch. The incoming current-key socket is rejected without association or SQL. Actual World::UpdateSessions removes the closing session.
native_modes.6: After a valid instance link queues one SQL result, real instance peer EOF marks teardown. Another current-key socket is rejected without association or another query. The retained ready result is discarded, and native world session cleanup closes the realm/removes the session.

method: Use actual loopback TCP transports, WorldSession/WorldSocket, accepted HandlePlayerLoginOpcode, native ConnectTo packet/RSA serialization and actual AddInstanceSocket enqueue. The fixture drains one native link-queue record into the real private ProcessLinkInstanceSocket to inspect admission before unrelated session updates; it does not replace the production dispatcher or model socket IsOpen/OnClose behavior.

Fixture instance type and enumerated character eligibility are seeded at the post-authentication boundary. The actual current connection key comes from production SendConnectToInstance. Rejected transports have no WorldSession association, so their real close must not set forceExit on the valid session.

Accepted links call native HandleContinuePlayerLogin and the entire LoginQueryHolder query set against schema-only scratch auth/character databases. The fixture retains the genuine ready SQL callback until duplicate/deadline controls are checked, then delivers it through the production query processor. Every successful path creates an ordinary Player and executes Map::UpdateSessions at99+1ms, preserving ObjectAccessor lookup, alive health321, exact recovery position, sickness15007 at598000ms and the original item25 GUID/durability27. Logout leaves health321/online0 and no Player/lookup/query.
limitations_and_pending_client_checks: No WoW client was used. This is not an end-to-end authentication or encrypted-wire test: login credentials/digests, auth continued-session SQL/HMAC, encryption acknowledgement, client ConnectTo handling and packet display are not exercised. The native socket admission boundary and actual TCP EOF are exercised.

Mode6 isolates rejection of a replacement link during teardown and deliberately discards its previously ready SQL result. It does not prove that an already-queued SQL response is skipped after disconnect. Existing session evidence retains the bounded completion-then-cleanup ordering; do not claim that behavior was changed here.
EOF is completed before link dispatch under fixture control. Concurrent IO/world-thread interleavings and generalized socket synchronization are not proven by this ordered regression.
The existing lightweight extracted-handler test remains useful for five-attempt bounds and queued client failure reports; its transport/session stubs do not substitute for these native socket tests.
Camera, movement, pet portrait, rapid interactive relogin, connection error presentation and quest traversal still require the7.3.5 client. No personal character/account data is used.
next_candidate: AbortLogin after a valid instance socket has attached but before its SQL response, followed by a new accepted request. The native cancellation cases here precede socket attachment; do not infer that later boundary is covered.
